title: Stationarity of a noise maximizer
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i>0$ and $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $1<p<2$ and $0\le\rho<1$. For $h:I\to\mathbb{R}$, define $G(h)=\sum_iw_i|h_i|^p$ and $F(h)=\rho^2\sum_iw_i h_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_i h_i)^2$. Suppose $g_i\ge0$ for every $i$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ for every $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ with $G(f)=1$. Then $F(g)\ge1$ and, for every $i$, $F(g)g_i^{p-1}-\rho^2g_i=(1-\rho^2)\sum_jw_jg_j$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $1<p<2$, and $0\le\rho<1$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $g_i\ge0$, $G(g)=1$, and $F(f)\le F(g)$ whenever $G(f)=1$, then $F(g)\ge1$ and $F(g)g_i^{p-1}-\rho^2g_i=(1-\rho^2)\sum_jw_jg_j$ for every $i$.
